events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
Under NS-0, this trip is routed by the branch that applies: cancelled_by = rider [F2], so the only fee clause that can be reached is the rider-cancellation branch, NS-4, and the 30-day dispute route in NS-7. The no-show clauses (NS-1/NS-2) are not engaged at all, because the driver never asserted a rider no-show, driver_arrived_at is null and driver_pressed_here_at is null [F3][F4][F8]. NS-1 is therefore never satisfied, and NS-0 leaves no other clause under which a cancellation fee could stand.

On the operative test, NS-4 charges nothing where the rider cancels within 3 minutes of matching. The timeline records acceptance at 12:54:00 and rider cancellation at 12:55:40 [F2], i.e. 1 min 40 s (100 s) after matching, which is inside the non-chargeable window. The $6.61 line item on record [F5][F2] is thus not chargeable, and NS-4's counterpart (NS-1) gives the driver no compensating entitlement: he never tapped "I'm Here" and never entered the pickup zone [F3][F4], and his closest approach was 2597 m [F1], so no $4.50 driver share or waiting item is earned under NS-1 or NS-6.

The environmental facts do not change this: traffic on the route was flowing normally with no incidents and fair weather [F9][F10][F11], which explains the driver's position as ordinary driving but does not create any chargeable item under NS-1 or NS-3; nothing here shows the driver refused, obstructed, or misreported anything.

Amount: the only figure to reverse is the cancellation fee actually charged, $6.61 [F5], cross-checked with the timeline entry [F2], with no surge component (1.0×) [F6]. No arithmetic beyond the recorded fee is required, and it follows the trace formula (cancellation fee $6.61). Under NS-7 the refund is issued as a Ryde voucher and remains subject to Ryde's discretion.

No account flag is warranted: the aggravated NS-2 button-abuse condition requires an "I'm Here" tap while off-location, and here there was no tap at all [F4], so NS-2's flag limb is not triggered. The driver's profile counts (3 disputes, 2 upheld, both no-show) [F13] are small-sample and cannot decide or add anything to this case, and RD-6 does not apply because this is not a route-deviation case and no RD-2 refund arises.

ruling.recommended_action: Reverse the $6.61 rider-side cancellation fee and issue a voucher for $6.61 under NS-7; no account action against the driver.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (12:55:40 vs accepted 12:54:00), i.e. within the 3-minute window, so under the rider-cancellation branch no cancellation fee is chargeable.

The $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F2, F5) was therefore not chargeable and must be refunded in full; the driver's written claim 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' (F8) does not create a fee, since the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' and no arrival was ever recorded (F3, F4).

Independently of the cancellation timing, the driver was 2597 m from the pickup point at 12:54:00 and never came within 200 m (F1), so the NS-1 no-show preconditions (driver at the pickup point, waited over 3 minutes) could not have been satisfied even if the driver had asserted a rider no-show.

No weakening factor exists in the environment: no incidents were recorded on the route and weather was fair (F10, F11), so the driver's distance from the pickup cannot be attributed to a documented obstruction.
The disputed amount to refund is exactly $6.61, taken from the recorded cancellation fee (F5, cross-checked with the timeline record F2), with no surge component (F6).

The driver's 90-day record shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld, both no-show cases (F13); combined with this case this supports sending the driver's account for review as an additional action, not as a basis for the finding itself.

weaknesses: My own case rests on the rider-cancellation branch (NS-4), and the complaint's framing that the driver 'was nowhere near' is not itself a defence under NS-4 — Ryde has published no rule granting a free cancellation because the driver is far away or late (the ETA-based waiver is an unincorporated informational clause, NS-8 (不可引用)), so the refund must stand solely on the 1-min-40-s timing fact F2.

The driver will argue he was en route and blameless, relying on his statement F8 and his otherwise busy, well-rated record (F13, 4.7 rating, 1160 trips); a judge inclined to protect the driver may treat the cancellation as the rider's choice rather than a Ryde error.

My flag_account request is thin: the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' at all (F4), so the aggravated NS-2 abuse-of-button flag (pressing 'Here' while off-location) is not triggered, and the profile counts are small-sample (F13) — the profile facts cannot decide the case and can only be an add-on.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled an instant (RydeX) booking just 1 min 40 s after matching, which is within the 3-minute window that Ryde treats as non-chargeable only where the rider-side fee is concerned; the $6.61 on record is the rider's own cancellation-fee line item and not a driver-initiated no-show charge.

The driver never pressed "I'm Here" and the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point, so no NS-1 no-show precondition was ever asserted by the driver; the driver did not claim the rider no-showed and no waiting-time item exists on this trip.

No in-app chat messages exist between the parties and the driver's only statement is "I was on my way when the rider cancelled"; nothing in the record shows the driver refused, obstructed or misreported anything toward the rider.

Traffic on the optimal route (KEPPEL ROAD speed band 4, 30-39 km/h) was flowing normally and no incident was recorded, so the driver's position 2,597 m from the pickup at acceptance is ordinary in-progress driving, not a fabricated arrival.

The $6.61 is a rider-side cancellation fee defined as $6.61 in Ryde's policy with no surge applied, so there is no computational or fare-basis error for the driver to answer for on the amount; any waiver is a rider fee-waiver question, not a driver misconduct finding.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 upheld no-show disputes, but the profile facts alone cannot establish any breach in this case, and no flag_account is warranted here because the driver never pressed "I'm Here" nor completed a trip without a rider aboard.

weaknesses: F1 (gps) is the rider's strongest fact: the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 2,597 m and he never entered the 200 m arrival zone, so the rider's claim that 'the driver was nowhere near' is factually correct and the driver cannot show any approach to the pickup in the 1 min 40 s before cancellation.

F3 and F4 (timeline) confirm driver_arrived_at is null and the driver never tapped "I'm Here"; if the judge reads the record as the driver having represented himself as able to serve the booking, the driver has no timeline evidence of any legitimate progress toward Marina Bay Sands to rebut it.

The rider's fee is $6.61 and the rider cancelled inside the 3-minute grace period; the rider will argue NS-4's 3-minute rule and NS-7's 30-day waiver route entitle her to a full refund (F2, F5), and the driver has no fare or gps fact showing he incurred cost in those 100 seconds.
F13 shows 2 upheld no-show disputes against this driver in 90 days, which the rider will use to argue a pattern under RD-6-style 'repeated' reasoning even though the profile cannot decide this case.

points.response: Conceded as a description of the record: the $6.61 is indeed the rider-side cancellation-fee line item (F2, F5). But that concession decides nothing for the driver — under NS-4 a fee charged on a cancellation 1 min 40 s after matching is not chargeable at all, so the line item must be reversed regardless of which party it was addressed to.

This is the driver's own case: because driver_pressed_here_at and driver_arrived_at are both null and the driver never asserted a rider no-show (F3, F4, F8), NS-1 can never be satisfied and NS-0 leaves no route to keep any $6.61. A fee with no supporting clause is a fee that falls away.

Absence of chat or misconduct is irrelevant to the fee: NS-4 makes any cancellation made within 3 minutes of matching non-chargeable without requiring rider misconduct, and the driver's 'I was on my way' statement (F8) is a statement that loses to the timeline records F2–F4.

Conceded that the driver was simply driving normally (F9, F10, F11) and no fabricated arrival is alleged in this case — but that is precisely why the driver incurred no compensable cost and no clause authorises the $6.61 he retained.

Agreed the amount is arithmetically $6.61 with no surge (F5, F6) — the error is not arithmetic but entitlement: NS-4 charges nothing inside 3 minutes, so the whole $6.61 comes back, and NS-7's 30-day route is satisfied because the dispute is filed now.

Conceded that the profile alone (F13) cannot decide this case, and I do not press the aggravated NS-2 button-abuse flag since F4 shows no 'I'm Here' tap. I maintain only that F13 (2 of 3 disputes upheld, both no-show) supports sending the account for review as an add-on to the refund, and the finding itself rests on F2–F5.

My C1 is reinforced by the driver's own concessions: the fee was charged on a cancellation 1 min 40 s after matching and the driver never asserted a no-show (F2, F3, F4), so no clause in NS-0 leaves the $6.61 standing and the refund must be full.

Conceded on the mechanic: the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2), inside the 3-minute window, and the $6.61 rider-side cancellation fee is therefore not chargeable under the rider-cancellation branch (NS-0, NS-4). My brief never disputed the timing or the amount (F5, F6); it disputes only whether any conduct finding against the driver follows from it.
